network.tdh.formal.metadataDescription: A Lean 4 model of the TDH rule, and what its proofs do and do not guarantee.
network.tdh.formal.title: Formal model
network.tdh.formal.lede: We are writing TDH-v1 a third way: as a precise mathematical model in Lean 4, a programming language in which a computer checks every step of every proof. This page explains what the model contains, what its proofs will establish and what they will not.
network.tdh.formal.why.title: Why write the rule again
network.tdh.formal.why.body: Plain English can be read two ways. When a second implementation was written from the specification alone, it found 23 places where it had to guess; two of them were rated high, because the two readings give different results. Each now has an exact rule.
network.tdh.formal.why.body2: A formal model leaves no such room: every term has exactly one meaning, and the computer rejects a proof with a gap.
network.tdh.formal.contains.title: What the model contains
network.tdh.formal.contains.body: The Lean model defines the same steps as the specification, one module per section. Its definitions run: the model computes TDH for a given input, so it can be tested on the same 36 conformance vectors as every other implementation.
network.tdh.formal.contains.status: Status today: the definitions are being written, module by module. No statement is proved yet, and the table below shows each one as planned until a published build says otherwise.
network.tdh.formal.module.caption: Modules of the model
network.tdh.formal.statements.title: What the proofs will state
network.tdh.formal.statements.intro: Each statement below is planned. The status column changes to Proved only when Lean’s kernel accepts the proof with no gaps.
network.tdh.formal.statements.manifest: Statuses from the Lean build of {date}, Lean {version}. The model reproduces {passed} of {total} conformance vectors.
network.tdh.formal.statements.caption: Statements, {shown} of {total} shown
network.tdh.formal.st.order.title: Order independence
network.tdh.formal.st.order.plain: The result depends only on which events are in the input, not on the order in which they arrive.
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.title: Copies are conserved
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.plain: For every card, the accounting neither creates nor loses copies except where the rule says so: mints add copies, the FirstGM burn is not credited, and the two sinks are never debited.
network.tdh.formal.st.netting.title: Netting
network.tdh.formal.st.netting.plain: A copy that leaves a wallet and returns within one transaction leaves that wallet’s holdings unchanged; A to B to C in one transaction equals A to C.
network.tdh.formal.st.carry.title: Age stays with its identity
network.tdh.formal.st.carry.plain: A copy keeps its acquisition time when it moves between wallets of one identity, and only then.
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.title: Last in, first out
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.plain: A send removes the most recently added entries of the sender’s list.
network.tdh.formal.st.days.title: Whole days
network.tdh.formal.st.days.plain: A copy’s whole days are never negative, and never fall from one day to the next while it stays.
network.tdh.formal.st.rounding.title: Rounding equalities
network.tdh.formal.st.rounding.plain: BASE equals the old two-step rounding; RATE and FINAL equal half-up except at exact ties; ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645 and ADD(n) = 144,051 from 33 sets; the boost’s rounding never meets a tie.
network.tdh.formal.st.boostBounds.title: Boost bounds
network.tdh.formal.st.boostBounds.plain: Under tdh-v1.0 the boost is between 1.00 and 2.24.
network.tdh.formal.st.identities.title: Identities
network.tdh.formal.st.identities.plain: Every identity is a group of at most three wallets in which every pair is confirmed both ways, and no wallet belongs to two.
network.tdh.formal.st.sums.title: Identity sums
network.tdh.formal.st.sums.plain: An identity’s base is the sum of its wallets’ bases, and its TDH is the sum of its per-token values.
network.tdh.formal.st.range.title: Range
network.tdh.formal.st.range.plain: Inside the tdh-v1.0 range every value fits in 64 bits, and binary64 evaluation equals the exact rule.
network.tdh.formal.st.conformance.title: Conformance
network.tdh.formal.st.conformance.plain: The model reproduces all 36 conformance vectors. This is checked by running them, not by proof.
network.tdh.formal.not.title: What the proofs will not guarantee
network.tdh.formal.not.english.title: That the English text says the same thing.
network.tdh.formal.not.english.body: People check that the model matches the specification; a disagreement is fixed in one or the other and recorded.
network.tdh.formal.not.programs.title: That the Rust and Python programs match the model on every input.
network.tdh.formal.not.programs.body: They are checked against the same 36 vectors and against each other every day, but no machine-checked proof links their code to the model.
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.title: That the inputs are right.
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.body: Whether a day’s Ethereum events are complete and genuine is checked by other means: every validator checks events against Ethereum’s block headers (D118), and two separately written programs prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s history (D119).
network.tdh.formal.not.rule.title: That the rule is the right rule.
network.tdh.formal.not.rule.body: A proof shows the rule does what it says, not that it is fair or wise. Rule changes are owner decisions.
network.tdh.formal.not.lean.title: Lean itself.
network.tdh.formal.not.lean.body: The proofs rely on Lean’s small kernel and its standard axioms. A proof that admits a gap is not counted as proved, and the table shows it.
network.tdh.formal.check.title: How you will be able to check
network.tdh.formal.check.body: The model is published with the validator code. Anyone with Lean installed can rebuild it, which re-checks every proof, and run the vectors through it.
network.tdh.formal.layers.title: Three layers of assurance
network.tdh.formal.layers.desc: The English specification is checked against the Lean model by people. The Lean model holds definitions and proved statements, the only machine-checked links. The programs, the Rust core, program B and the Python reference, share 36 vectors with the model and agree with each other daily. Inputs are checked separately, by checked reads and proofs A and B.
network.tdh.formal.layers.programsSub: Rust core, program B, Python reference
network.tdh.formal.layers.machine: Machine-checked: only the proofs inside the Lean model
network.tdh.formal.layers.human: Checked by people or by tests
